chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Nothing is slaughtered in Makkah except the camel, the cow, the sheep, and the chicken.
ai.seo_question: Which animals are permitted to be slaughtered in Makkah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific zoological boundaries for ritual slaughter within the Haram of Makkah, reflecting the juristic consensus that restricts valid sacrificial animals to those traditionally recognized in Islamic law. By explicitly listing camels, cattle, sheep, and poultry, it excludes wild game or other livestock, thereby preserving the sanctity of the sacred precincts from general hunting practices. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the permissibility of consuming meat slaughtered in Makkah versus the restrictions on hunting within its boundaries.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Nothing can be slaughtered in Makkah except for the camel, and the cow, and the sheep, and the chicken’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is prohibited to slaughter any animal in Makkah except camels, cows, sheep and chickens.”’
